title: First New Sunscreen Ingredient in More Than 25 Years Reaches U.S. Shelves
excerpt: Bemotrizinol — a sunscreen ingredient used for decades in Europe and South Korea — is the first new one cleared by the FDA in over 25 years, and the first products are now reaching U.S. shelves.
content:
For the first time in more than 25 years, Americans shopping for sunscreen have a genuinely new ingredient to choose from. Bemotrizinol — often shortened to BEMT — is the first new chemical sunscreen ingredient cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in over a quarter-century, and the first sunscreens made with it are now reaching store shelves, the Associated Press reported.

The FDA cleared bemotrizinol in June 2026. The first U.S. products containing it are now rolling out, including formulas from Neutrogena, and La Roche-Posay announced its Anthelios UV Defense SPF 50 with the ingredient on October 20, 2026.

Old abroad, new here

Bemotrizinol is not new everywhere: it has been used for decades in Europe and South Korea. Part of the reason for the long U.S. wait is regulatory — the United States regulates sunscreen as a drug, while some other countries treat it as a cosmetic. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary said the agency “has historically moved too slowly in this area,” according to the AP.

What makes it different

To be effective, sunscreens must protect against two kinds of ultraviolet light: UVB rays, which cause most sunburn, and UVA rays, which pose the greatest risk of skin cancer and wrinkles. Older U.S. formulas generally mix several ingredients to cover both. Bemotrizinol covers both UVB and UVA by itself. Dermatologists cited by the AP say the ingredient has decades of safety data behind it, is minimally absorbed into the skin, and does not leave the white streaks associated with some sunscreens.

Why it matters in South Texas

Laredo lives with intense, year-round sun, which makes news about sun protection directly relevant to Webb County readers. Cross-border shoppers may also already be familiar with the ingredient from sunscreen products sold abroad, where it has long been on the market.
